title.narrative: Increased capacity of Member States to develop and implement comprehensive employment policy frameworks and to mainstream employment into economic and investment policies

description.narrative: Increasing the capacity of Member States to develop and implement comprehensive employment policy frameworks is critical to a human-centred structural transformation that is conducive to job-rich growth and improved work quality in line with ILO Convention 122. The expected results include not only the development and application of these public policies but also their integration into broader economic plans which will foster sustainable development, in line with SDG 8. The final beneficiaries are working women and men worldwide, particularly in sectors poised for growth such as the green, care and the digital economies. Institutions benefiting include national and sub national governments and employer and workers organizations. The expected results include: (1) New research including on: planning for implementation of employment policies; financing of employment policies; evolving themes in employment policies; measuring employment impacts of investments and policies; the role of employment policies in supporting multiple just transitions; coherence between demand side policies; productivity and decent work; trade and investment; inequalities in the labour market. (2) Policy advice, guidance tools and other knowledge products relevant to different stages of the employment policy cycle, including on the green, digital and care economies. (3) Enhanced institutional capacity of constituents through training and peer learning in cooperation with the Turin Centre, including on diagnostics and employment impact assessments, policy design, implementation and financing. (4) Partnerships and advocacy for the promotion of Convention122, Recommendation 204, Recommendation 205 and the support for digitalisation in employment (in coordination with outcome 8).
